origin.description: Edition 1 pads a short row. Edition 2 glues extra fields into the last column. Python takes a callable.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The data, path, or collector this function accepts.

origin.details: Edition 1 pads a short row. Edition 2 glues extra fields into the last column. Python takes a callable.
origin.value: The same value readr 2.2.0 returns for this case, written as one line in the output.
origin.example:
first <- flatdf(with_edition(1, read_csv(I("1,2\n3,4,5"), col_names = c("X", "Y", "Z"))))
second <- flatdf(with_edition(2, read_csv(I("1,2\n3,4,5"), col_names = c("X", "Y", "Z"))))
paste(first, second, sep = " || ")

translation.description: Edition 1 pads a short row. Edition 2 glues extra fields into the last column. Python takes a callable.

translation.details: Edition 1 pads a short row. Edition 2 glues extra fields into the last column. Python takes a callable.
translation.value: The same value readr 2.2.0 returns for this case, written as one line in the output.
translation.example:
first = flatdf(with_edition(1, lambda: read_csv(I("1,2\n3,4,5"), col_names=["X", "Y", "Z"], show_col_types=False)))
second = flatdf(with_edition(2, lambda: read_csv(I("1,2\n3,4,5"), col_names=["X", "Y", "Z"], show_col_types=False)))
return first + " || " + second
